title: Dark Side
text: “Ohh, amazing, amazing!”

Ark seemed to be manipulating the rain of swords zipping through the air—loop the loop, was it?—like a yo-yo on invisible strings, I say. The swords flew along arcs aimed straight at Ren, tracing looping trajectories through the air. Mixed in among them were blade movements that seemed to possess a will of their own, and Ren fought quite literally inside a tornado of swords. He read the blade that dove into his chest, dodged it by a hair’s breadth, and struck back at Ren amid the deluge of swords swirling in every direction.
“Haaah!”

Ren deflected a sword that came flying at his back and tried to close the distance on Ark, only to be met with a great backflip that carried Ark clean out of reach. Quite the speed on that one, I say.
“Push it up another gear!”
“Not bad, not bad.”
Watching the exchange between Ark and Ren, I turned to Hou-kun and asked.
“That’s a rather serious training session going on there. Are you sure that’s safe, I wonder?”
“Looks that way, but Ren-kun doesn’t take any real damage when that cat cuts him.”
“Is that so, indeed?”
“Yep. That’s basically how the cat operates. Still, he’s pretty unusual too, isn’t he? Happily taking that kind of onslaught.”
Ren was laughing even as he fought. He looked utterly absorbed in the training. Glancing over at Éclair, I found her watching the spectacle with a dumbstruck expression.
“Ren has wanted to train under strange restrictions for a while now… but I never imagined he wanted to fight inside a literal storm of blades like this.”
“How does one even end up in a battle like this, I wonder?”

“Ah… we were doing morning practice when Ark and the others showed up, and Ren asked whether they could recreate the kind of combat he’d been having Gaelion help him with. At first it was just two floating swords, then three, then four, and before I knew it, it had turned into this… Ren just kept getting more and more heated, and here we are.”
So a training session meant to be assisted by Rival had escalated into this. And sure enough, that countless swarm of swords was all Ark’s doing.
“Well then… let’s kick it up a notch.”

No sooner had Ark said this than he seemed to grip each sword at once, shot past Ren’s side in an instant, and whipped around mid-backflip to slash at his neck and legs. Ren caught the blade—but just as I thought, ‘Now’s his chance to counter!’, Ark used one of the airborne swords as a foothold, dropped in a rapid dive, and pressed the attack even further. Remarkably nimble combat, I say. Ren, deflecting the swirling swords, swung his blade back at the diving Ark. Skills seemed to be off-limits, since Ren never used a single one.
“Haaaah!”
Ren let one sword drop—or rather, feigned dropping it—kicked the falling blade back up, caught it, and swung it at Ark’s head, stopping just short.
“Ohh… well done.”
In an instant, the swords swirling wildly all around vanished. Ren caught his breath with a sigh, then bowed to Ark.
“Can’t you add more swords? No need to hold back.”
“Want me to kick the gear up a bit more, then?”
“Yeah. At the very least, you should’ve been able to cut me five times during that jump. I want you to actually do it. I’d prefer it if I couldn’t win at all.”
“Wow, such a masochist… no thanks.”
Hou-kun teased Ren with that remark. And honestly, when it came to training, Ren really was a masochist through and through, always pushing himself to the absolute limit.
“You never know what might happen in this world. I’m glad things are peaceful now, but I still want to be prepared.”
Ren said this with a somewhat melancholy air.

“Fuhahaha! Ceaseless training amplifies the darkness! With power thus honed, we shall let the whirlwind of shadow roar across the world, offering up the wretched apostles who preach of light as sacrifices to the dark!”
Black Thunder cheered Ren on with great enthusiasm.
“…I’ll accept swinging my sword against those who hide behind justice to oppress the weak, but…”

As if he’d long since graduated from that sort of thing, Ren seemed unenthused by Black Thunder’s invitation, as always. Ah, I see—so Ren wasn’t the type to frolic about with little Kuro-chan on some loop while Big Sister came to collect him. That’s what I found myself thinking as I watched him. Just then, Ark tilted his head slightly, gazing at Black Thunder.
“You’ve been saying ‘darkness’ a lot just now—talking about sacrifices to the darkness and all that. But is that really something the darkness itself wants?”
“Indeed! The darkness lurks in the shadow of light, seeking sacrifice! Darkness remains darkness even without light! In other words, a world wrapped in darkness is our true world!”
Black Thunder was as fired up as ever today.

“Without light, darkness would have no way of knowing where it begins or ends—wouldn’t that be troubling for it? And having some unwanted, incomprehensible sacrifice thrust upon it, only to be blamed for the whole thing—wouldn’t that be a problem too? If you’re going to look at something, wouldn’t you rather gaze at happiness and joy than at the misfortune and sorrow that’s already lying around in excess?”
“Such naive sentiment has no place—”
Black Thunder tried to dismiss the notion outright, but after locking eyes with Ark, he fell strangely silent.
Watching the two of them stare each other down, Ren tilted his head, puzzled.
“Fu… how disappointing. Let’s leave the debate at that.”
For whatever reason, Black Thunder turned his back and walked away right then and there.
“I rather like the idea that darkness exists for the sake of peaceful sleep. The other aspects of darkness are nothing but sorrow, after all.”

Apparently, as Black Thunder later confided, he’d seen something like an abyss in Ark’s eyes. He claimed that though he’d thought he was merely indulging in edgy delusions, he’d somehow stumbled upon the genuine article, and that was what he’d glimpsed in Ark.
“There’s a saying, isn’t there? ‘When you gaze long into an abyss, the abyss also gazes into you.’”
“Without light, darkness loses track of where it ends and breaks down. Wouldn’t true darkness, deep down, wish more than anything for the triumph of light?”
I didn’t quite follow any of this—was this simply something only a god-slayer could understand, I wondered?
“I’m on the side of light, myself! Shining bright like the sun!”
“…That’s rather extreme.”
As expected of Hou-kun! Radiant and dazzling. Clearly Filolial-sama understood perfectly well that she belonged to the light side.
“Though light shouldn’t just grow bigger without limit either, mind you.”
“So basically, having nothing at all is bad, but too much brings its own kind of abnormality?”
“That’s right. That cat over there, us, and… even those other guys, carry a certain kind of contradiction, which is exactly why everything ends up so troublesome.”
“Contradiction, huh… I wonder about that.”
Ren and Hou-kun carried on with a conversation I couldn’t quite make heads or tails of.
“That annoying Black Thunder finally ran off… what a relief.”
“Well, he does seem to want to play with you, so why not indulge him a little?”
Ark said this to Ren with a cheerful chuckle, as if gently guiding him along.
“Even by Motoyasu-kun’s standards, that fight just now was full-on chuunibyou, though.”
Hou-kun sat down heavily, offering a rather world-weary commentary on Ren and Ark’s training session.
“Romance is meant to be enjoyed. It’s literally what they call a man’s dream, isn’t it? Ren-kun looked like he was having fun too, so why not play along with him? I’ll train with you again sometime.”
“Ah… yeah. Either way, train with me more!”
“You’re certainly enthusiastic about this.”
“…I just don’t want any more regrets. That’s all I want.”
Ren really had become quite serious of late. According to Father, Ren’s problem was that his sense of responsibility ran a bit too strong.
“Is there something in particular weighing on your mind?”
“…The spirit of the sword told me an opportunity would come, eventually. I want to train hard so that when it does, I won’t have any regrets.”
“Hmm…”
Ark and Hou seemed to be looking at something within Ren regarding all this.
“You two are god-slayers, right? Don’t suppose either of you has any idea how to deal with my regrets?”
“Unfortunately, your problem seems to fall outside my jurisdiction. Whatever’s weighing on your mind right now, it has nothing to do with those self-proclaimed gods.”
“You can tell that much?”
“The cat here and I can see a fair bit, you know.”
Apparently Ark and Hou-kun had some idea of what was troubling Ren.

“That said, I suppose I could lend a hand to someone working as hard as you. The aftertaste would probably be better that way. But for now, I think continuing your training is what’ll draw the better future toward you.”

The future branches off in countless directions, after all. And it’s painful not being able to choose the path you want, right when you want it. That’s how Ark answered—sounding, for all the world, like someone discussing college entrance exams.
